title: Insects: The Most Successful Animals
hook: By sheer numbers and variety, insects rule the animal kingdom — more than half of all known animal species have six legs.
key_points: Insects make up over half of all described animal species — more than a million kinds.
Three body parts, six legs, and usually wings define the insect body plan.
Their small size, fast breeding, and flight let them fill nearly every habitat.
A tough exoskeleton protects them and limits water loss on land.
Insects pollinate plants, recycle waste, and feed countless other animals.
content_html: If you measured success by variety and sheer numbers, insects would win the animal kingdom hands down. More than half of all described animal species are insects — well over a million kinds, with many more still unnamed. Beetles alone outnumber every group of vertebrates combined. Their basic design is unmistakable: a body in three parts, six legs, and, in most, a pair or two of wings.
extra_html: As Encyclopaedia Britannica notes, several features explain this runaway success. Insects are small, so a single leaf or crack in the bark can be a whole world to them, letting many species share one habitat. They breed fast and in huge numbers, so populations recover quickly and evolution can act rapidly. Most can fly — they were the first animals to do so — which lets them escape danger, find food, and colonize new ground. A tough outer exoskeleton shields their bodies and slows water loss, a crucial advantage on dry land. In return, insects do essential work: pollinating flowering plants, recycling dead matter, and forming the base of food webs that countless other animals depend on.

related.hook: Sponges, spiders, sharks, and squirrels look nothing alike — yet all are animals, sharing a few deep traits that set them apart from plants, fungi, and microbes.

related.title: Vertebrates and Invertebrates
related.hook: The animal kingdom splits along one simple line: do you have a backbone or not? The vast majority of animals don't.

related.hook: A caterpillar becoming a butterfly is one of nature's great transformations — many animals reshape their bodies entirely as they grow up.

flashcards.prompt: Why are insects considered the most successful animals?
flashcards.back_html: They are the most diverse and numerous animals — over half of all known animal species are insects, thriving in nearly every habitat on land.

flashcards.prompt: How many legs does an adult insect have?
flashcards.explanation_html: Insects have six legs, attached to the middle body section (the thorax) — a feature that distinguishes them from eight-legged spiders.

flashcards.prompt: What trait helps insects survive and spread across so many habitats?

choices.text: Small size, fast breeding, and the ability to fly
Living only in the deep ocean

flashcards.explanation_html: Being small, quick to reproduce, and able to fly lets insects exploit tiny niches, colonize new areas fast, and bounce back quickly from setbacks.
